content: The WikiDoc Foundation is a non-profit organization classified under section 509(a)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code. Donations made to the foundation are tax-deductible. Overview The WikiDoc Foundation relies entirely on the charitable contributions of its viewers. It does not accept financial support from pharmaceutical companies or medical device manufacturers. Allocation of Funds Currently, all donated funds are used to cover the operational costs of the website, specifically the server bandwidth. There are no paid employees at this time, and all efforts to maintain the foundation are carried out on a voluntary basis. How to Donate by Credit Card or PayPal If you choose to donate using a credit card, the transaction will be processed through PayPal. The charge will appear on your credit card statement as WikiDoc Foundation. After making a donation, you will have the option to print a receipt for your records and for tax purposes. If you would like a receipt mailed to you, please provide your address so that we can send confirmation of your donation. How to Donate Using an IRA Individuals who are 70½ years of age or older can make a direct, tax-free transfer of up to $100,000 per year from their IRA to an eligible charitable organization, such as the WikiDoc Foundation. This provision, established under recent legislation, allows donors to support a charitable cause while avoiding taxes on funds that the IRS would otherwise require to be withdrawn and taxed. For further assistance with this type of donation, please contact us. How to Donate Using a Charitable Remainder Trust (CRT) Charitable Remainder Trusts (CRTs) and Grantor Retained Annuity Trusts (GRATs) provide an opportunity for property owners (e.g., those with buildings, land, or equipment) and high-net-worth individuals to transfer assets to the WikiDoc Foundation. These mechanisms can significantly reduce the tax burden on heirs while supporting the foundation.
